HdfRequirementChangeEvent.title: HDF Requirement Change Event
HdfRequirementChangeEvent.description:
A single continuous-monitoring wire event: one requirement's effective posture changed on one system component.

The streaming increment of a systemDrift hdf-comparison — events fold into comparisons and reassemble into hdf-results, they never mutate documents in place.

One event per wire document (NDJSON-friendly).

The envelope (identity, ordering, hash chain) is the shared Change_Event_Envelope primitive; the payload carries the producer-computable change state, a thin before projection, and the full after requirement (the evidence a responder opens the event for).

Design: ADR-0005.

requirementId.description: Canonical requirement identifier — the same identity as Requirement_Diff.id and the requirement's id in hdf-results. Together with the envelope's (systemRef, componentId) this forms the durable entity key. A requirement renumbering is emitted as absent + new under the two keys, never an in-place key change; batch comparison reconciles renames via its oldId/newId matching.

state.description: The producer-computable subset of Requirement_State: new | absent | updated | fixed | regressed. fixed and regressed carry the direction SARIF's baselineState lacks; project down to SARIF's closed 4 values for external interop.

changeReasons.description: Why the state changed. An overrideExpired flip is a different triage than resultChanged: the control did not get worse, a waiver lapsed.

before.description: Thin projection of the prior effective posture, for at-a-glance alerting without a state-store lookup. Null exactly when state is new (no prior posture exists). The full prior state is recoverable from the consumer's materialized state; the envelope's priorChecksum covers the integrity of that recovery.

after.description: The full requirement as evaluated after the change — required and non-null for every state except absent (null there: the requirement left the assessment scope). Full content is load-bearing twice over: reassembly parity (applyChangeEvents cannot reproduce changed result content from a projection) and triage (the failing results[] ARE the 'why' a responder opens the event for).

HdfRequirementChangeEvent.$comment: Examples, in order: 1) fixed — the common remediation event: a failing SSH FIPS-cipher control was fixed and rescanned. priorChecksum is the effectiveChecksum of the prior failed posture; after carries the full passing requirement including its new effectiveChecksum (the next chain link); 2) regressed via overrideExpired — the waiver that held this control at passed lapsed, so effective posture regressed to failed with NO new scan finding. A different triage than resultChanged: renew or remediate. priorChecksum is the waived posture's checksum; the expired override remains in statusOverrides as the audit record; 3) new — a requirement entered assessment scope (chain start for this key): before is null, priorChecksum is null. The full after payload is what makes the new key materializable by applyChangeEvents; 4) absent — the requirement left assessment scope (component decommissioned or benchmark rule retired): after is null by definition; the thin before preserves the last observed posture for downstream views; 5) updated via impactChanged — a riskAdjustment override lowered effective impact while the control stayed failed: status unchanged, so neither fixed nor regressed. after carries the override and the recomputed effectiveChecksum over the adjusted posture.

APIKeyExchangeRequest.title: API Key Exchange Request
APIKeyExchangeRequest.description: Exchanges an API key for a short-lived bearer token. The key never travels to a service route; only the token does.

resource.description: RFC 8707 audience, required for the same reason as on the oauth2 grant.

scope.description: Space-delimited subset of the key's registered scopes.

DocumentCreated.title: Document Created
DocumentCreated.description: The id a submitted document was stored under, and its content digest.

id.description: Opaque. A caller addresses the document by this and nothing else.

sha256.description: Digest of the submitted bytes. Advisory, and the secondary key for idempotent re-ingest (Zalando #231) rather than an identifier a caller may address.

IngestRequest.title: Ingest Request
IngestRequest.description: Any one of the eight HDF document types, submitted whole. The response is the id the document was stored under.

TokenRequest.title: Token Request
TokenRequest.description: OAuth 2.0 client-credentials token request. Sent as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, per RFC 6749; `resource` is required rather than optional so every issued token names the API it is for (RFC 8707).

grant_type.description: The only grant this API issues tokens for.

client_secret.description: Sent in the form body rather than a header, as RFC 6749 §4.4.2 permits.

resource.description: RFC 8707 audience. Required: a token with no named audience can be replayed against any resource server that trusts the issuer.

scope.description: Space-delimited subset of the closed scope vocabulary. Omitted means the client's full registered scope set.

TokenResponse.title: Token Response
TokenResponse.description: An issued bearer token and the scopes it actually carries.

token_type.description: Fixed; the API advertises one http/bearer scheme.

expires_in.description: Seconds from issue. Absolute expiry is in the token, not here.

scope.description: Space-delimited scopes GRANTED, which may be narrower than those requested — a client must read this rather than assume it received what it asked for.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Extension members are permitted; the 403 carries `scope`.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota for the active window, as a structured field.

RateLimit-Policy.description: The quota policy this endpoint applies.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token. The deployment advertises its authorization server through RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource.
